video_title: Toronto Raptors Media Availability | Practice | October 7, 2026

quotes.speaker: Kelly Olynyk
quotes.summary_phrase: Kelly Olynyk compares current Raptors team to his Memphis Grizzlies
quotes.excerpt: reminds me a lot of my teams in Memphis where we were super close off the court
quotes.quote: It reminds me a lot of my teams in Memphis where we were super close off the court. You can see the camaraderie with the young guys. They all click, they like each other. Off the court, the weight room, joking around, talking to each other. We spent a lot of the summer together. That just always leads to wins, good chemistry on the court, being able to handle success, being able to handle losses.
quotes.social_post: Kelly Olynyk sees strong parallels between this year's Raptors and his past Memphis teams, noting that the camaraderie built off the court is already translating to chemistry on the floor.

quotes.speaker: Kelly Olynyk
quotes.summary_phrase: Kelly Olynyk on Jamal Murray's ability to impact the game
quotes.excerpt: Jamal was one of my favorite players to watch in the league. Every time I would watch
quotes.quote: I watched them a lot last year. Honestly, Jamal was one of my favorite players to watch in the league. Every time I would watch him, he was able to affect the game without scoring, something that I do. So I just enjoyed watching him, how they play hard, play together, always looking to get in the gaps and the passing lanes. I enjoyed watching them last year.
quotes.social_post: Kelly Olynyk says he spent time studying Jamal Murray last season, specifically admiring how the guard impacts the game without needing to score.

quotes.speaker: Kelly Olynyk
quotes.summary_phrase: Kelly Olynyk praises Darko Rajaković's attention to detail
quotes.excerpt: He is so keyed and locked in on the details that it is tough as a player
quotes.quote: I think that is just in his nature to help guys get better. He is so keyed and locked in on the details that it is tough as a player to see the whole landscape. I think he does a great job of seeing that and what will help you get better in the game. And then he does a great job of relaying the message to you. Some coaches have trouble relaying the message or what they want. He does a great job with all that stuff.
quotes.social_post: Kelly Olynyk praises Darko Rajakovic for his attention to detail, noting that the coach excels at relaying complex concepts to players in a way that is easy to understand.

quotes.speaker: Kelly Olynyk
quotes.summary_phrase: Kelly Olynyk on his veteran role with the young Raptors team
quotes.excerpt: help out the young guys. It is a long season. You do not want to get too high
quotes.quote: I think he wants me to come in here and use my veteran experience, help out the young guys. It is a long season. You do not want to get too high or too low. We have done two years together, so we have been through a lot. I think he knows that I know a few things about the regular season and the postseason. He just wants me to come in here and be vocal, not necessarily be a leader, but be there for the young guys with whatever I can help.
quotes.social_post: Kelly Olynyk on his role with the young Raptors: He is focused on using his veteran experience to guide the team through the highs and lows of the season while being a vocal presence.

quotes.speaker: Kelly Olynyk
quotes.summary_phrase: Kelly Olynyk on playing the five position
quotes.excerpt: I spoke to Darko about that. He said I need you to be ready to play the five
quotes.quote: I spoke to Darko about that. He said I need you to be ready to play the five, maybe handle the ball, things like that. He is focused on that. If I am comfortable there, I think the game has shifted to kind of a small-ball five at times, so I am comfortable doing whatever I have to do on the court.
quotes.social_post: Kelly Olynyk confirms he has discussed playing the five with Darko Rajakovic, noting he is ready to handle the ball and adapt to the small-ball lineups required in the modern NBA.

quotes.speaker: RJ Barrett
quotes.summary_phrase: RJ Barrett on his versatility and role
quotes.excerpt: just kind of being all over, whether it is rebounding, defense, just being in the right spots
quotes.quote: It is just kind of being all over, whether it is rebounding, defense, just being in the right spots, cutting, catch and shoot. He does a lot of things. He is very versatile, so we will see once once he gets back.
quotes.social_post: RJ Barrett emphasizes the importance of versatility, focusing on rebounding, defense, and spacing as he prepares for the upcoming season.

quotes.speaker: RJ Barrett
quotes.summary_phrase: RJ Barrett on learning the team's new points of emphasis
quotes.excerpt: It is cool to have those guys coming in and talk to us a little bit about
quotes.quote: It is cool to have those guys coming in and talk to us a little bit about the rules and stuff and just kind of what to expect. I am still going to do what I do, but it is good to know like there are certain points that that they are looking for.
quotes.social_post: RJ Barrett says the team is currently adjusting to new points of emphasis and rules provided by the league, though he remains focused on his own playing style.

quotes.speaker: RJ Barrett
quotes.summary_phrase: RJ Barrett on Immanuel Quickley's positive energy
quotes.excerpt: Some people just have good energy, man. And it is every day. You almost wonder how is he
quotes.quote: Some people just have good energy, man. And it is every day. You almost wonder how is he doing this every day like that. Most people have a bad day. No, he comes in smiling energy every single day. He is just a good guy, bro. Obviously he works hard, he works hard for us on on the court, but other than that, like coming in, he is he has been leading and just everybody loves having a guy like him around. He is like the team the team favorite guy. Everybody love him.
quotes.social_post: RJ Barrett calls Immanuel Quickley the team favorite, highlighting his infectious energy and work ethic as a constant positive force in the locker room.

quotes.speaker: RJ Barrett
quotes.summary_phrase: RJ Barrett on playing for the Canadian national team
quotes.excerpt: I think when you represent your country, it is a little bit of a different pride
quotes.quote: I think when you represent your country, it is a little bit of a different pride because one we are not playing for any money anyways. And two it is just yeah, it is like there is a world I am from. I love Canada, so for me playing for the Raptors, I think playing one in the chip here, probably mean the world to me. It would be different because it is here, but in either regard, your country, you are always going to play for them. So that is just a certain level of pride that that you take in doing that and trying to represent your country, you would do that for no money at all.
quotes.social_post: RJ Barrett on representing Canada: It is a different level of pride that you take in doing that and trying to represent your country, you would do that for no money at all.

quotes.speaker: Darko Rajaković
quotes.summary_phrase: Darko Rajaković on Kyle Filipowski's leadership and coachability
quotes.excerpt: Kyle is always about the right things. He is a very coachable player
quotes.quote: During open gym every time that we played live, he is not shying away from from, you know, talking to the guys. And you can call that mentorship, leadership, you can call them keeping each other accountable, whatever it is. Kyle is always about the right things. He is a very coachable player. This is not his first rodeo, this is not his first team. He is trying to integrate it in a system and to understand his teammates and to see what are the biggest gaps that he can help in. But his voice is being heard right away with our team and our guys have a lot of respect for him.
quotes.social_post: Darko Rajakovic says Kyle Filipowski is already making an impact in training camp, noting that the rookie is vocal, coachable, and has earned the respect of his teammates.

quotes.speaker: Darko Rajaković
quotes.summary_phrase: Darko Rajaković on his relationship with Kyle Filipowski
quotes.excerpt: I always like loved Kyle. I always like engaging with him
quotes.quote: I always like loved Kyle. I always like engaging with him. I was not as assistant coach, I was not responsible for daily work with him, so he was not my guy, call it that way. But we always had good conversations. I do remember when during COVID, fellow co-coach Taylor Jenkins was out and I was a substitute teacher for for a couple of games. And the first game that we played, we played against Golden State. It was a great game and end of the game, I drew up a play for us to inbound the ball because we needed to save it. And it was not a great play, but Kyle was smart enough to to flash into right position, catch the ball, we got a dunk on that play and everybody were saying, oh, look at coach, he has got a great play.
quotes.social_post: Darko Rajakovic shares a story about his early coaching days, recalling how a smart play by Kyle Filipowski helped bail out a drawn-up play during a game against Golden State.

quotes.speaker: Darko Rajaković
quotes.summary_phrase: Darko Rajaković on building a team with versatile players
quotes.excerpt: The way we build teams in Europe, you sign point guard, then two guard, then three guard
quotes.quote: The way we build teams in Europe, you sign point guard, then two guard, then three guard, then four, and five, and everybody knows their positions. And every time that you draw a play, you say one, two, three, four, five, and everybody knows who is who. And for us is Scotty starts at four, but then he moves to one, then he becomes a five. And Kawhi is three, but a different lineup, he becomes a four. It is very interchangeable. And what it does is the way we wanted to develop our system that is going to take a minute, it is not easy, is that all of those players that can make plays off of each other and understand each other's tendencies and what they do well.
quotes.social_post: Darko Rajakovic explains his vision for a positionless Raptors offense, where players like Scottie Barnes are expected to be interchangeable and make plays for one another.

quotes.speaker: Darko Rajaković
quotes.summary_phrase: Darko Rajaković on rookie injuries and the learning process
quotes.excerpt: I see that a lot with rookies, you know, when they come first time to NBA
quotes.quote: I see that a lot with rookies, you know, when they come first time to NBA. It is, you know, I don't want to say that it is because we go in training camp and it is extremely hard or what not, just different kind of physicality. All of those guys coming from college, they walk into NBA, doesn't matter the talent, that player that walks into NBA and court, he is not going to be most physical or or the best player at the time. And for all for all and it is it is learning what it takes at this level, to how you need to practice every day, what treatment means, how you need to take care of your body.
quotes.social_post: Darko Rajakovic discusses the physical adjustment rookies face in the NBA, emphasizing that learning how to practice and take care of their bodies is the biggest hurdle for newcomers.

quotes.speaker: Darko Rajaković
quotes.summary_phrase: Darko Rajaković on integrating Kyle Filipowski into the rotation
quotes.excerpt: I think he has a lot of intangibles that can help our team right away
quotes.quote: I think he has a lot of intangibles that can help our team right away. We are still in training camp, all of those games they they are now for a first of us evaluating all the options that we have. And I think that he is absolutely competing for for a spot on in rotation right away. And you know me, I am not shying away from throwing rookies out there on the court. I love to see, you know, you cannot learn how to swim until you get jumping in the water. You got you got to throw those guys in the water and like, you know, slowly teach them how to swim.
quotes.social_post: Darko Rajakovic confirms Kyle Filipowski is competing for a spot in the rotation, adding that he is not afraid to throw rookies into the fire to help them learn.
